subject: Conversion corridor: enablement matrix & engineering kickoff
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Conversion corridor: enablement matrix & engineering kickoff

Hi Ben, Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the streaming and tool-calling demo really mapped to a lot of our immediate needs. Per our product team's request, we're trying to accelerate the first-phase feature enablement that includes: streaming real-time notes, function/tool calling for our slot-filling flows, and a structured JSON output for our downstream analytics pipeline.

To move fast, we sketched a short checklist and a preferred rollout runway attached (HB_onboarding_checklist_v1.xlsx). High-level asks:
- Confirm the JSON schema contract we should use for initial delivery (sample schema attached: hb_json_schema_v1.json).
- Agree on a mutual action plan (MAP) and kickoff time for engineering pairing.
- Identify any compliance/retention nuances for streaming traces.

Would you be available for a 45-minute engineering kickoff on Friday morning PST? If possible, include a person from your runtime/serving team and your CS lead so we can triage the schema edge cases live.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Product
HealthBridge AI

Attachments: HB_onboarding_checklist_v1.xlsx, hb_json_schema_v1.json
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conversion corridor: enablement matrix & engineering kickoff

Emily — thanks for the clear backlog. Friday 10:00 AM PST works for us; I scheduled a 45-minute block and invited the people below. Quick notes before the kickoff so we can use the time for decisions, not discovery: 

1) Scope split (what we'll aim to ship in phase 1):
   - Streaming: server-side server-sent events (SSE) for low-latency token streaming to your UI; prefix caching enabled.
   - Function/tool calling: declarative schema + invocation framework; we'll propose an idempotent retry pattern for external tool calls.
   - Structured outputs: agreed root-level JSON envelope per your schema; we'll propose a versioning strategy (v1/v2) to avoid runtime mismatch.

2) Data & retention: Redwood hosted mode will hold ephemeral KV/cache for 24 hours by default; production contracts can extend or change retention. We noted you wanted 90 days for traces — please confirm if that applies to token-level traces or only aggregated logs.

3) Pre-kickoff deliverables (we attached a mutual action plan draft to the invite):
   - HealthBridge: final list of critical fields in schema + example prompts that must produce <status> and <codes>.
   - Redwood: proposed schema compatibility report and a minimal runtime config (batching, quantization profile) to hit your latency targets.

Attaching the MAP draft: MBP_mutual_action_plan.pdf and linking a Miro board where we'll map the conversation.

See you Friday — I've looped Lauren (Solutions Engineering) and Marissa (CS) to lead the implementation runway.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MBP_mutual_action_plan.pdf
Links: https://miro.com/app/board/uXjH-example-board
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthbridge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conversion corridor: enablement matrix & engineering kickoff

Emily — thanks for the checklist; Ben thanks for the MAP. Ahead of our 10:00 AM slot I'm dropping a concrete implementation matrix and a minimal schema compatibility guide so engineering can pair on a versioned contract instead of re-authoring during the call.

Key artifacts attached: hb_json_schema_v1.json (sample), plus a short implementation matrix below.

Implementation matrix (phase 1) — owner / acceptance / target:
- Streaming (SSE, continuous tokens): Lauren / Redwood runtime / acceptance = end-to-end token latency < 300ms on 99th pct / target = 3 weeks to prod parity
- Function calling (stateless tool invocation): HealthBridge + Redwood SE / contract test harness / acceptance = successful call + idempotent retry across 3 failure modes / target = 2 weeks after kickoff
- Structured JSON (v1 envelope): Shared (spec below) / agreement on schema fields / acceptance = no parsing errors in downstream pipeline + sample payloads passed

Minimal schema compatibility guide (excerpt):
- Top-level envelope: {"version": "v1", "session_id": "string", "payload": { ... }, "tool_calls": [ ... ] }
- Required payload fields for phase 1: timestamp(string, ISO8601), note_text(string), confidence(float between 0 and 1), diagnostics(object optional)
- Tool call object: {"tool_id": "string", "inputs": { ... }, "status": "succeeded|failed|retrying", "result": { ... } }

Please review the attached hb_json_schema_v1.json and flag any required fields that must be considered non-optional for HIPAA-like retention decisions. Also note: we've added a low-overhead debug trace header that can be toggled per-session to avoid long-term storage defaults.

See you in 55 minutes.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: hb_json_schema_v1.json
From: Implementations <implementations@healthbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conversion corridor: enablement matrix & engineering kickoff

Thanks team — the kickoff was productive. HealthBridge confirms the following next steps and approvals: 

1) Schema: Approved with two required additions (patient_id hashed string, and source_channel enum). We'll provide a short addendum by Monday.
2) Trace retention: We accept Redwood's default ephemeral token retention but request aggregated traces retained for 90 days; please include this in the SOW as a line item.
3) Timeline: Phase 1 target is 3 weeks for streaming parity and 2 weeks for tool-calling tests after the kickoff (aligned with your implementation matrix).
4) Contract: Emily will route a redline for a one-off SOW amendment to cover trace retention and a short SLA for high-priority calls. We expect to have the signed SOW in ~7 business days pending internal approvals.

We'll upload the sample payloads and addendum to the Drive folder you shared. Attaching a stub SOW template for reference.

— HealthBridge Implementations
Implementations Team
HealthBridge AI

Attachments referenced: HB_SOW_stub.docx
